title: Sections with support: the sheaf-level adjunction
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible (one of the condensed coefficient rings specified in
[sk-def-localizing-closure]), let $X$ be a standing scheme, and let
$i\colon Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with open complement
$j\colon V\hookrightarrow X$. Use $\Lambda_Z=i^{-1}\Lambda_X$ and
$\Lambda_V=j^{-1}\Lambda_X$ as coefficient rings
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]). For
$M\in\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ put
$\underline\Gamma_Z(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$, where $M\to j_*j^*M$ is the
unit of $j^*\dashv j_*$.

1. $\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)=i_*\underline\Gamma_Z(M)$, naturally in $M$.
2. $\underline\Gamma_Z\colon\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
   is right adjoint to the exact functor
   $i_*\colon\Mod(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$;
   in particular it is left exact and preserves limits.
3. $\underline\Gamma_Z$ sends K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes,
   and injective modules to injective modules.

proof.text: The standing schemes are separated and of finite type over the standing field, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the whole ring. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. In a Noetherian affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$, an arbitrary open cover of $V\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$ refines to basic opens $D(g_a)$. The ideal generated by all these $g_a$ is finitely generated, so finitely many of the original $g_a$ already generate it: express finite generators as finite sums and collect the finitely many elements occurring. A prime contains these finitely many elements exactly when it contains every $g_a$, so their basic opens still cover $V\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$. This proves quasi-compactness of $j$ on affine charts. Here the affine-chart meaning of Noetherian and finite generation are [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The coefficient morphism $\alpha_f$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] is an isomorphism of ring objects. Consequently the module functors of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] are the ringed-site inverse and direct images with the inverse-image coefficient rings in the statement. We can apply arbitrary-ring-sheaf results with $B=\Lambda_X$, rather than treating $\Lambda$ as a discrete constant ring.

source.place: opening paragraph: standing scheme, quasi-compact open complement and coefficient identifications; Stacks 01T6 (morphisms.tex, lemma-finite-type-noetherian)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with the commutative ring sheaf $B=\Lambda_X$ and the complementary immersions. It supplies exact $i_*$, $i^*i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$, $j^*i_*=0$, and the canonical localization sequence $0\to j_!j^*F\to F\to i_*i^*F\to0$. The exactness of $i^*$ and $j^*$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. To check also the actual open counit, use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison] to identify $j^*$ with restriction to the slice at $V$. For a module sheaf $H$ on $V$ and an object $W\to V$, the direct-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives $(j_*H)(W\to X)=H(W\times_X V)=H(W)$, since $V\to X$ is a monomorphism. The restriction adjunction's counit is this identification on sections, hence is an isomorphism. Uniqueness of a left adjoint to the specified direct image identifies this adjunction with $j^*\dashv j_*$, including its counit. Thus its counit $\varepsilon_H:j^*j_*H\to H$ is invertible. Likewise the closed counit is the isomorphism given by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-closed-counit], so $i_*$ is fully faithful: for a map $i_*A\to i_*B$, transpose along $i^*\dashv i_*$ and compose with the inverse of the counit at $A$ to obtain its unique preimage $A\to B$.

Put $N(M)=\ker(\eta_M:M\to j_*j^*M)$. The triangle identity is $\varepsilon_{j^*M}\circ j^*(\eta_M)=\operatorname{id}_{j^*M}$. Since the counit is invertible by step 2, $j^*(\eta_M)$ is its inverse. Exactness of $j^*$ from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] therefore gives $j^*N(M)=0$. The localization sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applied to $N(M)$, becomes $0\to0\to N(M)\xrightarrow{q_M}i_*i^*N(M)\to0$. Hence $q_M$ is an isomorphism, proving (1), where the equality in the statement means this canonical identification. It is natural: for $f:M\to M'$, the unit square induces the unique kernel map $N(f)$ with $\iota_{M'}N(f)=f\iota_M$, and naturality of the closed unit gives $i_*i^*N(f)q_M=q_{M'}N(f)$.

source.place: (1): apply open restriction to the kernel and then the localization sequence

proof.text: Given a $\Lambda_Z$-module $A$ and $\phi:i_*A\to M$, transpose $\eta_M\phi$ under the module adjunction $j^*\dashv j_*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Its source on $V$ is $j^*i_*A=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], so the transpose, and hence $\eta_M\phi$, is zero. There is a unique $\widetilde\phi:i_*A\to N(M)$ with $\iota_M\widetilde\phi=\phi$. Full faithfulness of $i_*$ from step 2 gives a unique $\psi:A\to i^*N(M)=\underline\Gamma_Z(M)$ with $i_*\psi=q_M\widetilde\phi$. Conversely send $\psi$ to $\iota_M q_M^{-1}i_*\psi$. Kernel uniqueness and full faithfulness show that both composites are the identity. Precomposition in $A$ and postcomposition in $M$ commute with this construction, because $q$, $\iota$, and the adjunction bijections are natural and the kernel factors are unique. This gives the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*A,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,\underline\Gamma_ZM)$, proving the adjunction in (2).

source.place: (2): explicit kernel factorization, full faithfulness and inverse Hom correspondence

proof.text: The kernel maps defining $N$ preserve identities, compositions and sums, by composing with the monomorphisms $\iota_M$ and using their uniqueness. Since $i^*$ is additive, $\underline\Gamma_Z=i^*N$ is additive. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits] to the adjunction just constructed: $\underline\Gamma_Z$ preserves every small limit in the fixed sheaf universe. In particular it preserves zero objects and kernels, and thus is left exact in the abelian module categories of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. This completes (2).

source.place: end of (2): right adjoints preserve limits; Stacks categories.tex, Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), part (2)

proof.text: The exact functor $i_*$ of step 2 preserves monomorphisms, by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a). Apply [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to $i_*\dashv\underline\Gamma_Z$. For each injective module $I$ on $X$, this gives injectivity of $\underline\Gamma_Z I$ on $Z$. This proves the module assertion in (3), without any constructibility or boundedness restriction.

By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], the additive adjunction of steps 4-5 induces $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(Z)}(C,\underline\Gamma_Z I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(X)}(i_*C,I)$ for arbitrary integer-indexed cochain complexes. If $C$ is acyclic, exactness of $i_*$ and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](c), applied at each degree, give $H^n(i_*C)\cong i_*H^n(C)=0$. If $I$ is K-injective, the right-hand Hom group is therefore zero. As this holds for every acyclic $C$, [def-pur-kinjective-complex] says precisely that $\underline\Gamma_Z I$ is K-injective. This proves the remaining assertion of (3), including unbounded complexes.

split_report.summary: Split the existing three-clause sheaf theorem into seven checked steps, reusing arbitrary-ring-sheaf recollement and generic categorical tools. No new nodes. Replaced a dangling Cartesian-coefficients reference by the existing coefficient-morphism isomorphism statement; preserved the hypotheses and conclusions. Made the actual open counit, kernel naturality, the two directions of the Hom bijection, and unbounded K-injectivity explicit. Existing project Lean covers only the constant-ring adjunction, not all clauses for condensed admissible coefficients.
split_report.blueprint: Opening recollement paragraph: steps 1-2; clause (1): step 3; clause (2): steps 4-5; clause (3): steps 6-7. This follows the current sk-lem-formal-closed-support unit route.
